text:
Shane Pinto spent his 26th birthday scoring twice against Colorado, the second one in overtime. "A Cool Day," as the Senators' video put it. It was part of a strong start: 9 goals and 17 points in 24 games, at 20:10 a night, a top-line workload.

The shooting percentage, 20.5%, looks like a number due to fall, and some of it will. But his expected goals are right there with the actual ones (9 goals on 8.6 expected), because he keeps shooting from the dangerous spots. That's why our numbers rank him 20th of 554 skaters in wins added from his goals.

The worry is quieter. He's pointless in four straight, though on 2.9 expected goals, so the chances haven't gone anywhere. And Ottawa's 5v5 shot share is worse with him on the ice than off it, by almost 7 points. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he plays with strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers. If the drought ends soon, the goal pace (our middle projection is 28) is the story. If the line keeps bleeding shots, that's the one to watch.
headline: Pinto's scoring is real, the quiet stretch too
